article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Evening Brief
article.dek: Justin Jefferson is out for Sunday, Friday's final injury designations are in, and the evening cards rotate back to Chicago — with the Value lane finding plus-EV on the Dolphins.

items.headline: Justin Jefferson is officially out Sunday
paragraphs: The morning question got its answer. Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday that Justin Jefferson is OUT for Sunday's home game against the Dolphins (4:05 p.m. ET). The star receiver sprained his left ankle in last week's win over Tampa Bay, missed practice all week, and couldn't get there in time. O'Connell says Jefferson is 'definitely feeling better' and the goal is to have him practicing next week ahead of Week 5 at New Orleans.

With Jefferson sidelined, Jordan Addison becomes Minnesota's top target after catching five passes for 90 yards and a touchdown in relief last week, and Jauan Jennings moves up a rung. Cornerback Charles Demmings (hamstring) and punter Brett Thorson (hamstring) are out too.
items.takeaway: The morning's big tell resolved — plan Sunday without Jefferson.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Bears: Caleb Williams (hamstring) and left tackle Braxton Jones are officially OUT, so Case Keenum starts against the Jets on Sunday — the app already projects him, so this is confirmation, not a surprise. D'Andre Swift practiced Friday and carries no designation.

49ers: Nick Bosa (knee/calf) is out, along with two more defensive linemen. Mike Evans (ribs), Dre Greenlaw, Keion White, and Jaden Dugger are questionable. Trent Williams was cleared. Ravens: Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ronnie Stanley (toe) are questionable; Trey Hendrickson is out for finger surgery; Lamar Jackson has no designation. Patriots: Christian Gonzalez and Christian Barmore are OUT in Buffalo. Packers: Aaron Banks, Jacob Monk, Warren Brinson, and Anthony Campbell are out; Edgerrin Cooper (concussion) practiced fully Friday and is questionable. Cardinals: Josh Sweat (groin) is questionable after a new Friday injury. Dolphins: Caleb Douglas, Robert Beal Jr., and Storm Duck are out; Jaylen Wright will play. Giants: nobody questionable, nobody out.
items.takeaway: Friday's designations are the last full picture — the only thing left is the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Sunday weather: an early look
paragraphs: Rain looks likely around kickoff in Philadelphia (Rams at Eagles, mid-60s) and Baltimore (Titans at Ravens, mid-60s). There's a chance of showers at MetLife (Cardinals at Giants) and in Charlotte for the Sunday night game (Lions at Panthers). Tampa will be hot and humid near 90 with storms possible in the afternoon. Buffalo, Chicago, Cincinnati, Seattle, and Santa Clara look calm and dry. London (Colts at Commanders, 9:30 a.m. ET) is partly cloudy in the upper 60s. The dome and roofed games are unaffected.
These are Friday forecasts — the final kickoff-window numbers land in Saturday's editions. And a reminder: weather is a fact, not an edge. Totals are the app's weakest lane.
items.takeaway: Wettest windows: Philadelphia and Baltimore. Everything else is manageable.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The cards rotated back to Chicago
paragraphs: Hit Rate is Bears moneyline at -176 on FanDuel. The app gives Chicago about a 70% chance to beat the Jets — that's what Hit Rate is: which supported pick looks most likely to win. It gives up value to buy win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. That's not a flaw. It's the job.

Balanced is Bears -3.5 at -104, also FanDuel. The app puts Chicago covering at about 50.5%. That's the middle ground: a strong pick without paying too much. If you're new, Balanced is the good starting point. Two Chicago cards, two different jobs — pick the job you want.
items.takeaway: The card follows the price — tonight the most-likely-to-win read is Chicago again.

items.headline: The Value lane found its plus-EV play
paragraphs: Value is Dolphins +10.5 at -110 on FanDuel, and it's the only card on the board the app grades plus-EV (+1.48%). The app gives Miami about a 50.6% chance to cover in Minnesota.

Plus-EV means the price is better than the app's fair number — it does not mean Miami is more likely to win, or even more likely to cover than the other cards. An edge is a price thing, not a prediction thing. -110 means every $1.10 you risk wins $1. That's the whole mechanic. Your actual stake comes from your bankroll and the app's staking settings, which are deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Value is the model's price-beats-market read — it promises an edge, not a win.

items.headline: Quarterback check: the app is current
paragraphs: Before tonight's write-up, the board's expected starters were checked against Friday's news: Case Keenum (Bears), Jameis Winston (Giants), Marcus Mariota (Commanders), and Cam Ward (Titans, the starter) all match. No QB surprise is hiding off the board tonight.

If your book's line has moved off the board's number — or your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel — tap Check in the app. Type in your book's line and price. The app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Your book's number, not the board's — Check prices your actual ticket.

items.headline: What moved since the morning board
paragraphs: Hit Rate rotated: the morning read was Bills moneyline at -298 on DraftKings; tonight it's Bears moneyline at -176 on FanDuel. The most-likely-to-win card moved teams and books.

Balanced held: Bears -3.5 at -104 on FanDuel, same number, same price as the morning — though the evaluator's EV slipped a touch on the identical read. Value rotated off the Bears spread entirely and onto Dolphins +10.5 at -110, the board's plus-EV play. All three cards changed or moved. The board is alive, not sticky.
items.takeaway: The moves are in the board — bet your book's number, not the board's.

items.headline: Questionable is not out
paragraphs: Friday's designations are labels, not lineups. Questionable players suit up all the time — Edgerrin Cooper went from concussion protocol to a full Friday practice. The final word is the inactive list, about 90 minutes before kickoff. That's when Sunday's real lineup locks.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: No verified public-vs-sharper split surfaced on NFL games tonight, so here's the vocabulary for when one does. Handle (HND) is the share of MONEY on a side. Tickets (BET) is the share of BETS. When they point at opposite sides — lots of small bets one way, most of the money the other — that's a disagreement worth watching. When they agree, like tonight's free featured college row where both favor Virginia Tech, it's just popularity. Popularity is not information.
items.takeaway: Agreement is popularity. Disagreement is the thing to watch.

items.headline: The tracker only works if you're honest
paragraphs: Settlement is manual — nothing auto-grades your tickets. Log tonight's bets win or lose, including the ones you'd rather forget. A tracker with only winners in it is a diary, not a record.
